# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

New entries go in [`changes/unreleased/`](changes/unreleased/), one file per PR; see [`changes/README.md`](changes/README.md).

## [1.11.9] - 2026-10-28

### Fixed

- **A `clean` proxy verdict that graded no components is no longer reused under `fail_closed`** (#3396, #5043, #5056). Proxy scan verdicts are stored per content digest and shared by every repository that serves those bytes. A `clean` verdict with no findings and no cataloged components (for example one written by an on-demand rescan in a repository of another format) says only that the scan saw nothing it could grade, so a `fail_closed` download no longer serves from it: the bytes are scanned again as for a first pull, and a download whose identity cannot be established stays withheld (423). A conda download still reuses such a verdict when a conda repository recorded it, so a conda package with no Python or recognised binary content (such as `tzdata`) is scanned on its first `fail_closed` pull only; other bytes whose own grade catalogs nothing are scanned on each `fail_closed` pull. A rescan in a conda repository of a cached object that is not the package its file name declares follows the same catalog rule as below. A `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/security/proxy-scans/rescan` in a repository whose format does not scan on proxy (for example `generic`) in which the scanner catalogs nothing and finds nothing is now inconclusive: it answers 503 `RESCAN_SCAN_FAILED` and records no verdict, instead of recording `clean`.

- **Proxied package archives with two entries at one path are refused before the scan-on-proxy identity check** (#5050, #5052). The check that ties a proxied package to the coordinate it is served as reads the first matching manifest in the archive (`package/package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `*.nuspec`, `pom.properties`, `info/index.json`), while the extraction that unpacks the archive for the scanner keeps the last entry at a path, and a zip entry repeated as `./name` or `a//b` was read under one name and extracted under the other. An archive whose non-directory entries repeat a path, in the container or, for a conda `.conda`, across its payload tars, no longer establishes an identity: under `fail_closed` it is withheld (423) and under `fail_open` it is served `pending`, unscanned and unrecorded, as an unreadable archive is. A survey of 1,282 published packages across npm, PyPI, RubyGems, crates.io, NuGet, Maven Central and conda-forge found no outer archive with a repeated path.

- **CI OIDC exchanges mint a token that lives the configured access-token TTL instead of dying with the CI platform's ID token** (#5054, #5057). `POST /api/v1/auth/ci/token` capped the minted access token at the presented assertion's own `exp` (#3820). GitHub Actions ID tokens live about five minutes, so every token exchanged from GitHub Actions stopped working after about five minutes, whatever TTL was configured, and longer build steps failed with 401. The assertion now only has to be valid when it is exchanged, as with AWS STS, GCP Workload Identity Federation, Azure, PyPI trusted publishing and Vault, and the minted token lives the configured access-token TTL (`JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY_MINUTES`), at most one hour. An expired assertion is still refused, the mapping's repository ceiling and group binding still apply, a CI service account still cannot mint API tokens, and its session cannot be refreshed (the exchange returns no refresh token, and `/api/v1/auth/refresh` and the registry refresh grant now refuse CI accounts). `kubernetes` providers are unchanged: their pull-only credential still expires with the ServiceAccount token. Jobs that run longer than the TTL exchange a fresh ID token again; see `docs/ci-oidc.md`. 1.12.0 makes the lifetime a per-provider setting.

- **A virtual conda channel's package allowlist now applies to its hosted members too, so the channel no longer serves packages outside its list** (#5055, #5058). The allowlist (#4576) filtered only what remote members contributed: hosted (local and staging) members passed through unfiltered in the merged index and on downloads, so a hosted package appeared on every channel containing its repository whether or not the list admitted it. The list is now the channel's boundary for every member, in every index form a virtual serves (`repodata.json` plain, `.zst` and `.bz2`, the CEP-16 shard index and its shards, `current_repodata.json`, `run_exports.json`, `channeldata.json`) and on package and attestation-sidecar downloads through the virtual, with the same matching rules as before (name glob, version spec, subdirs; filename and record identity must agree). A hosted package the list does not admit is dropped and still owns its name, so the upstream's packages of that name stay excluded. Reads of the hosted repository itself are unchanged. A new `scope` field on `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/allowlist` restores the old behaviour per channel: `"scope": "remote_only"` (the default is `all_members`); a request that omits `scope` keeps the stored scope.

  **Upgrade impact:** on a channel with an enabled allowlist, hosted packages that are not on the list disappear from that channel (its index and downloads through it) until they are added to the list, or until the channel is set to `"scope": "remote_only"`. Check each virtual conda channel with an allowlist before upgrading. The hosted repositories themselves keep serving those packages directly.

### Security

- **pulldown-cmark moved to 0.13.5** (#5038). The crate is a build-time dependency of `prost-build`, which formats doc comments of the checked-in `.proto` files; it is not linked into the backend, so this clears a dependency audit finding with no runtime change.

- **The bundled grype and the scanner adapter's bundled trivy now link go-jose v4.1.6, published as scanner adapter 1.5.2** (#5041, #5042, #5049). go-jose v4.1.5 carried an upstream advisory that failed the image publish gate on both binaries. No grype or Trivy release carries the fix yet, though both upstreams have made the bump on main. The grype build stage in the backend and Alpine backend images adds a guarded go-jose override next to its x/net override, and the adapter's trivy moves from `ghcr.io/artifact-keeper/trivy:0.76.0-r2` to `0.76.0-r3`, the same upstream Trivy v0.76.0 with the same override. The Trivy release is unchanged, so a self-run Trivy server stays on 0.76.0.

## [1.11.8] - 2026-10-28

### Fixed

- **A proxy rescan that cannot grade a package archive leaves the stored verdict unchanged** (#3396, #5030). `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/security/proxy-scans/rescan` has no request coordinate to pin, so for the objects the download gate grades only through a pin or a staged image (npm tarballs, PyPI sdists, gems, crates, NuGet packages and OCI image manifests) a rescan whose scanner cataloged no components is now inconclusive: it answers 503 `RESCAN_SCAN_FAILED` and keeps the stored verdict, instead of recording `clean`. For every format, a rescan that finds no vulnerabilities no longer replaces a stored `vulnerable` verdict when it cataloged fewer components than that verdict was graded on; that is inconclusive too.

- **Accept an API token presented as a Bearer credential at `/v2/token`, so Renovate and other clients that configure a bare token can list Docker tags** (#4903, #4977). The exchange previously recognized only JWTs in that slot and answered 401, which surfaced as a failed `tags/list` request.

- **LDAP web login keeps an administrator's deactivation of an account** (#4933, #5029). A successful directory bind on the web LDAP login used to set a deactivated account active again. LDAP accounts now keep `is_active` across a federated login, the login of a deactivated account is refused, and an administrator must reactivate the account explicitly.

- **NuGet V3 search now aggregates package versions across virtual repository members and reports the latest stable SemVer** (#4976, #4979). A virtual NuGet repository combining multiple V2 remotes previously kept whichever member's result arrived first and applied V3 package paging to V2 version rows before grouping, so search could show an arbitrary older version and omit versions from other members. Search now groups version rows before paging, merges duplicate package IDs and their version lists, recalculates the root version with the requested prerelease policy, and preserves the available version entries.

- **Chunked uploads honour the repository's upload quarantine hold** (#5003). An artifact committed through `PUT /api/v1/uploads/{id}/complete` into a hosted repository with the upload quarantine enabled is now held, as an artifact uploaded through the format's native route is.

- **Chunked uploads apply the storage quota unless the session is a trusted replication session** (#5003). The quota check when a chunked upload session is created and the quota admission when it completes now exempt a session only when it is a replication session of an administrator or service account, as other replication-specific behaviour on the chunked upload path already required.

- **A repository's security score no longer goes stale when two of its scans finish at the same time** (#5006, #5007). Each score recalculation read the repository in its own snapshot with no coordination, so when two scans completed together one recalculation could store a score computed before the other scan had committed, and the other failed with a serialization error that nothing retried. The grade and severity counts then ignored the finished scan until the next scan in that repository, which could show as a false F. Recalculations of one repository now run one at a time under a database advisory lock and are retried on a serialization failure, so the stored score always includes every completed scan. This covers every path that recalculates a score: scan completion, finding triage, SBOM ingest and external findings ingest.

### Security

- **Update zstd to 0.14.3** (#5023). `zstd` moves from 0.14.2 to 0.14.3 and the async compression codecs (`async-compression` 0.4.49, `compression-codecs` 0.4.44) move onto the same zstd 0.14 / `zstd-safe` 8.2 stack, picking up the upstream fixes for RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398 and RUSTSEC-2026-0403. An older zstd 0.13 copy stays in the tree through `rattler_package_streaming` and wasmtime's compilation cache; the affected functions are not reachable through either, and the advisories are ignored in `.cargo/audit.toml` until those crates move to zstd 0.14. Lockfile-only; no behaviour change.

## [1.11.7] - 2026-10-24

### Fixed

- **`PUT /api/v1/peers/{id}/network-profile` now routes to the peer network-profile handler instead of returning a 500 with a raw axum extractor error** (#4884, #4906). The router had been mounted at `/peers/network-profile` without the `:id` segment; it now requires the peer ID, rejects malformed IDs with a normal 400, and returns 404 for an unknown peer.

- **Label moves and late format metadata now reach push peers** (#4889, #4899). The protobuf `_labels` index was a zero-byte row that the sync worker had nothing to transfer, and the NuGet, PyPI, Debian and nested-layout RPM routes queued their push before writing the format `artifact_metadata`. The label index is now stored as a real JSON object (with a refreshable, content-addressed row) and queued like any other upload, and those four routes queue after their metadata is committed; the metadata-diff re-arm now covers every format, so a worker that finished a transfer before the document landed redelivers it. Client-uploaded `maven-metadata.xml` remains intentionally row-less and unpushed: peers regenerate it from the versioned artifacts they receive rather than accepting one deploy's snapshot over their own generated view.

- **Concurrent first Maven uploads of one immutable release coordinate can no longer leave the winner's row pointing at the loser's bytes** (#4892, #4897). The object is now written inside the publishing transaction while holding the per-key publish lock, and an upload that finds the coordinate already published under that lock returns 409 without touching the winner's storage key; previously both uploads wrote the same object before either row was inserted, and a loser whose write landed last replaced the winner's bytes while its own row was rejected. The write happens before the repository-wide quota and usage-ledger row locks are taken, so other uploads into the same repository do not wait on it. In Artifactory migration path mode a hosted Maven artifact upload now writes its object once instead of twice (#4893).

- **A retried OCI blob completion no longer fails with 409 "upload session is already being modified"** (#4902, #4919). When a reverse proxy timed out the final `PUT ?digest=` of a large layer (Envoy and Envoy Gateway cut at 15 s by default) or the client dropped the connection, the backend abandoned the completion mid-way and left the upload session locked for six hours, so the identical `PUT` that containerd 2.x re-sends after a 504 was refused and the push failed. The completion now runs to its end even when its request is dropped. A retry with the same digest waits for it (up to `OCI_UPLOAD_COMPLETION_RETRY_WAIT_SECS`, default 30 s) and gets the same result, or 503 with `Retry-After` while it is still running; a retry after it finished gets 201; a retry with a different digest is still 409. A session held by a replica that died is reclaimable after five minutes instead of six hours. See `docs/operations/oci-reverse-proxy-timeouts.md` for the proxy timeouts to set.

- **The rollback guide now warns that a 1.11.x database cannot serve a 1.10.x backend for OCI pushes** (#4915, #4917). Migration 243 (1.11.0, #3851) replaced the unique key on `oci_upload_cleanup_keys` that the 1.10.x upload path names in `ON CONFLICT (storage_key)`, so after a rollback to 1.10.x with `SKIP_MIGRATIONS=true` every `docker push` failed with "there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification". `docs/operations/rollback.md` now says so up front, lists migration 243 in a new table of releases that cannot be rolled back across, and widens its boundary condition to dropped or replaced unique constraints.

- **Protobuf commits now replicate to push peers** (#4921, #4934). A protobuf (BSR) commit row recorded the commit digest as its `checksum_sha256`, so the receiving peer, which verifies the pushed bundle against that value, refused every commit push with 409 "checksum mismatch". New commit rows record the sha256 of the stored bundle (the commit digest stays the row's version and is still what every lookup uses). Rows written before this release need no operator step: the sync worker recomputes the sha256 from the stored bundle before pushing such a row and stores the corrected value. A push that the peer refuses for that one artifact (a checksum mismatch, or an immutable path already occupied) now fails only that task and no longer puts the whole peer into retry backoff; connection errors and 5xx responses still back the peer off as before.

### Security

- **`crypto-bigint` bumped 0.7.5 -> 0.7.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0387** (#4941, #4940). `crypto-bigint` 0.7.5 could take secret-dependent branches in some operations intended to be constant-time. It reaches the backend through the `bergshamra` XML signature crates. A second copy, 0.5.5, stays in the tree through `elliptic-curve` 0.13 (`pgp` and `bergshamra`) because the 0.5 line has no patched release; the advisory is ignored in `.cargo/audit.toml` until those crates move off it (#4940). Lockfile-only; no behaviour change.

## [1.11.6] - 2026-10-23

### Fixed

- **The PyPI age gate no longer blocks old releases whose filename spells the version differently from the Warehouse release** (#4907). The gate looked up a distribution's publish time by the exact version string in its filename, but Warehouse keys `releases` by the release's own spelling, so `cuda_toolkit-13.0.3.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl` (release `13.0.3`, uploaded months earlier) found no publish time and was withheld with a 451 indefinitely, which broke `pip install torch==2.14.1` on Linux. The lookup now falls back to PEP 440 equality on the download path and in both simple-index listing filters; a version that is not PEP 440-equal to a release still has no publish time and stays gated.

- **Two replication tests no longer race the background push queue** (#4911). The NuGet and nested RPM echo tests added for #4792 read `sync_tasks` before the spawned task that queues the client upload's push had written its row, so they failed intermittently in CI. They now wait for that task to settle before asserting. Test-only change; no production code changed.

### Security

- **`ctutils` bumped 0.4.0 -> 0.4.5 for RUSTSEC-2026-0385** (#4910). `ctutils` 0.4.0 generated masks and compared `u128` values in non-constant time. It reaches the backend through `crypto-bigint` under the `bergshamra` XML signature crates. Lockfile-only; no behaviour change.

## [1.11.5] - 2026-10-23

### Fixed

- **Chunked uploads through `/api/v1/uploads` now replicate to subscribed push peers** (#4791). The generic finalize path wrote its own `artifacts` row and never queued a push sync task, so a completed chunked upload only reached a peer after a manual sync; it now fans out like every direct and format-native publish, without re-queueing peer replication writes.

- **Peer replication no longer echoes NuGet and nested-layout RPM writes, and a pacman signature or conda attestation added after its package now reaches push peers** (#4792). Follow-up to #4725. The NuGet push handler and the `repodata_depth > 0` branch of the RPM upload queued push sync tasks even for a write that arrived from a peer (`X-Artifact-Keeper-Replication: true`), so the write was pushed out again to every push peer of the repository; both now skip the fan-out like every other format. A pacman `.sig` and a conda CEP-27 attestation are stored in their package's metadata, and uploading one queued nothing, so a peer that had already received the package never got it. Attaching one now delivers the package again with its new metadata (the finished push task is re-armed, and a push that was in flight when the signature or attestation arrived is re-armed when it finishes).

  On the receiving side, a trusted peer pushing the exact bytes that are already live at a path is now accepted as a replay that refreshes the artifact's metadata, instead of being refused with 409 as an immutable republish. Client uploads of identical bytes to an occupied coordinate are still refused, and a peer still cannot change the bytes of a released coordinate. A peer running an older release keeps refusing the replay, so the signature or attestation reaches it only after it is upgraded.

- **`ak_db_pool_connection_failures_total{stage="startup"}` is now exported** (#4828). The startup connect retry added in 1.11.2 (#4549) counted every failed initial connect attempt, but the database pool was built before the Prometheus recorder was installed, so those increments went to the `metrics` crate's no-op default recorder and the `startup` series never appeared on `/metrics`. The recorder is now installed before the pool is built, so a replica that needed several attempts to reach the database reports them once it is up. The `request` series was not affected.

- **A remote conda channel serves a CEP-16 shard again once its upstream does, after refusing it for not matching its address** (#4829). Since 1.11.0 a shard whose upstream bytes do not hash to its address is answered with 502, but those bytes had already been written to the proxy cache under the shard's path, which is cached as immutable and never revalidated. After the upstream recovered, the remote, and every virtual over it, kept answering 502 for that shard without asking the upstream again until the cache entry was evicted by hand.

  A shard is now checked against its address before it is committed to the proxy cache, and only a shard that matches is stored. A cached shard that does not match (one stored by an earlier release) is evicted on the next request and fetched again, so an affected cache heals without operator action. Both cases count in `ak_proxy_cache_checksum_mismatch_total`.

- **A failed hosted Maven upload no longer leaves its bytes behind** (#4837). A hosted upload stores the file before the transaction that records it, so when that transaction failed (a metadata write error, a quota refusal, a failed POM read) the client got an error while the object stayed in storage. On object storage those orphaned bytes were then downloadable through the repository's storage fallback, serving a deploy the server had rejected. The upload now removes its object when the publish does not commit, on every storage backend, and the object-storage fallback no longer serves an artifact coordinate that has no catalog row (checksum sidecars and `maven-metadata.xml` are still served from it). The cleanup is serialised against an overlapping upload of the same coordinate, so a failed upload can never delete the bytes of a concurrent one that succeeds.

- **Deleting a versioned Generic or MLModel repository now removes the objects of its older revisions as well** (#4865). The delete collected storage keys only from the repository's live `artifacts` rows. Older revisions live in `artifact_versions`, which no `artifacts` row names, and those rows cascade away with the repository, so the history objects stayed on filesystem and object storage with nothing left to derive them from, and the storage GC orphan scan, which starts from `artifacts`, could never find them. The key set now unions the repository's live artifacts and its own revisions under the same location-scoped sharing guard, and a revision key the delete spares because another repository still names it is handed to the storage-GC candidate set so the next GC pass reclaims it once no reference remains.

- **A plugin install or reload whose git source redirects to a blocked address is now refused with a 400 instead of a 500** (#4869). The outbound SSRF policy refuses two things under two different wordings: a host that resolves to an address the policy blocks ("blocked by SSRF policy") and a redirect hop that points at one ("redirect target rejected by SSRF policy"). Only the first was recognized when a git clone failed, so a source that redirected onto a blocked address fell through to the generic internal-error branch and the API answered 500 for what is a rejected request. Both refusals are now recognized through one shared vocabulary, so the plugin install and reload paths answer 400 with the same policy wording as the connect-time refusal, and an upstream fetch whose redirect the policy refuses is reported as the 503 the policy refusal deserves instead of a generic 500. No security change: the redirect is still aborted before the target is contacted.

- **A CRAN repository of type `remote` now proxies the upstream `PACKAGES`/`PACKAGES.gz` index, so R clients pointed directly at it can discover and install packages** (#4877). The source index was built from locally-catalogued rows alone, and a proxy repository only ever has rows for packages already fetched through it, so `GET /cran/{repo}/src/contrib/PACKAGES` answered an empty `200` even though the upstream (e.g. `https://cran.uib.no/`) publishes a full index; only individual package downloads were proxied, so `install.packages()` had nothing to resolve against. A remote repository now fetches the upstream `src/contrib/PACKAGES` (falling back to `PACKAGES.gz` for mirrors that ship only the gzipped form) and merges it over the locally-held rows, preserving every upstream DCF field, `Depends`, `Imports`, `LinkingTo` and the rest, because R resolves the dependency graph out of those. A locally-held package still wins its `(Package, Version)` slot, since its row carries the coordinates the download route serves from storage. An upstream that publishes no index (`404`) is not an error, but a genuine upstream failure with nothing held locally is now surfaced instead of being masked as an empty `200`.

- **A virtual conda channel merges each subdir once for every encoding and keeps serving the previous merged repodata while it rebuilds** (#4879). `repodata.json`, `.zst` and `.bz2` of one subdir were three independent merges (three member fetches, three merges, three encodings), and when a remote member's cached repodata expired the kept merge was dropped, so every request waited on a full rebuild: about 45 s for a conda-forge `linux-64` `.bz2`, which ended in `merge shed` 503s and client timeouts when a dozen subdirs refreshed at once. The merged `repodata.json` is now kept once, zstd-encoded, and `.json` and `.bz2` are derived from it on first demand and kept with it (each encoding keeps its own ETag; the plain `.json` of a virtual is now compact JSON). A kept document that is no longer fresh is served at once, with `Warning: 110`, while exactly one background merge rebuilds it, and the next request after the rebuild gets the new document, with the encodings the previous one had been asked for already built. The new `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MERGE_MAX_STALE_SECS` (default: the merge cache TTL) bounds how long after it was first found stale a document may still be served; `0` restores waiting on the rebuild. A merge with a failed member is never served stale. Stale serves count as `ak_conda_virtual_merge_cache_hits_total{via="stale"}`. See `docs/operations/conda-virtual-merge-memory.md`.

- **`AK_PROXY_METADATA_BUDGET_BYTES` above 4 GiB is now honoured instead of being silently clamped, so the conda virtual merge cap grows with it** (#4881). The buffered-metadata budget counted one semaphore permit per byte, and a reservation is taken through tokio's `acquire_many`, which takes a `u32`, so the budget was clamped to 4294967295 bytes with no log line: an operator who set 32 GiB got a 4 GiB budget, and the default `CONDA_VIRTUAL_MAX_CONCURRENT_MERGES`, derived from it, stayed at 3. The budget is now accounted in 4 KiB units (a reservation rounds up to a whole unit), so any value the platform can address is represented and 32 GiB yields `budget_bytes: 34359738368` and 28 default merges at the default member ceilings. A blank, non-numeric or zero value still falls back to the 1 GiB default, and that, or a value too large to represent, now logs a warning at startup naming the configured and effective values.

### Fixed

- **The migration jobs list reports `pagination.total` for the rows its `status` filter matched** (#4800). `GET /api/v1/migrations?status=failed` already narrowed the rows on the page, but the `COUNT(*)` behind `pagination.total` was computed without the filter, so a filtered view reported every job the caller could see and `total_pages` — the page count and "N of M" figure the UI derives from it — was too large. The count now carries the same filter as the listing; unfiltered totals are unchanged.

- **NuGet V2 upstream translation no longer drops XML entities and text before them in description/authors** (#4816). When parsing V2 OData feeds, character/entity references (`&amp;`, `&#xF6;`) and CDATA sections were treated as separate events that overwrote field values; the parser now accumulates text across `Text`, `GeneralRef`, and `CData` events before committing to the field.

- **S3 storage reindex no longer reports artifacts with non-ASCII or reserved characters in their path as missing** (#4817). On S3 storage, object_store writes such a path under a percent-encoded object key (`uni-1.0-café.jar` is stored as `uni-1.0-caf%C3%A9.jar`), and listing returned that stored key unchanged, so `POST /api/v1/admin/repositories/{key}/reindex-storage` reported the row's object as missing and counted the object as an unregistered ghost that a non-dry run would register a second time under the encoded path. S3 listings, including the `S3_PROVIDER=oss` REST fallback, now return keys in the form reads and writes use, which also lets proxy-cache purges and RPM version retention delete such objects. Existing object keys are not rewritten. An object written by another tool under a key that Artifact Keeper can neither read nor write (for example a raw `~`) is left out of the listing with a warning.

- **Members of the `repository-owner` role pass the repository `admin` check again** (#4818). Since 1.11.0 the repository administration routes (email subscriptions, the staging release target, upstream auth, egress proxy, routing rules, upstream filter, conda allowlist, PyPI tracks, the age gate and per-repository security settings) answered 403 to a `repository-owner` member, including the user who created the repository, because the check read fine-grained permission rules only and ignored role assignments. It now uses the same resolver as the write and delete checks, so a role carrying `admin` on the repository is honoured; `developer` and `reader` members are still refused.

- **Logout now revokes the session's refresh token even when the refresh token is not in the request** (#4831, GHSA-4x56-5942-m4fv). `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` revoked the refresh-token family only when the request carried the refresh token, in the body or the `ak_refresh_token` cookie. A bearer logout with an empty body, and a browser logout from the web UI, carry neither, so logout answered 200 while the session's refresh token kept minting new access tokens until it expired. Access tokens minted with a refresh token now carry that session's family id, and logout revokes the presenting session's family whether or not the refresh token is included. Other sessions of the same user stay signed in, as before. Access tokens issued before upgrading carry no family id; a logout with one of them behaves as before until the session next refreshes.

- **Concurrent uploads to one artifact path now agree on a single winner** (#4832). An upload to a path that already holds a live artifact at the same version is refused with 409 `CONFLICT` ("Artifact version already exists and is immutable") unless the repository has versioning enabled. That check ran before the bytes were stored and outside the transaction that writes the artifact row, so several `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/artifacts/{path}` requests racing to one free path could all pass it: each was answered 201, and the last to commit silently replaced the content the others had been acknowledged for. The same rule is now part of the row write itself, for direct uploads and for chunked-upload completion: exactly one of the racing uploads is answered 201 and keeps its bytes, and every other one gets the documented 409. A deleted artifact can still be replaced, and a versioning-enabled Generic or Mlmodel repository still appends a revision. The 409 is now listed in the OpenAPI description of the PUT.

- **Deleting a repository on filesystem storage now removes its files even when another repository holds the same bytes** (#4833). Generic and other content-addressed artifacts share a storage key across repositories that hold the same content, and the delete spared any key another repository's row also named. On filesystem storage each repository keeps its own copy in its own directory, so the other repository's copy wrongly shielded this one, the cascade then dropped the only row that named it, and garbage collection could never find it again. The check now counts only a repository that resolves the key to the same object (same backend, and on filesystem the same storage path), including an older revision there. A key the delete still spares because it is genuinely shared is handed to the storage-GC candidate set, so the next GC pass reclaims it once no repository references it, which also covers two repositories sharing a key on cloud storage being deleted together. GC likewise reclaims a trashed filesystem copy while another repository serves its own copy of the same key.

- **Server-side S3 copy of a large object with a non-ASCII or reserved character in its path no longer fails with `NoSuchKey`** (#4838). object_store stores each key segment percent-encoded (`café` is stored as `caf%C3%A9`), and S3 URL-decodes the `x-amz-copy-source` header once before looking the source up. The multipart `UploadPartCopy` path, which every object above `S3_MAX_SINGLE_COPY_BYTES` takes, encoded the caller's key instead of the stored one, so the header decoded to a key that does not exist. The header is now the URL encoding of the stored key, the same value object_store's single-request `CopyObject` sends for a small object.

- **The repository list and the repository update response now report a Remote's upstream authentication** (#4851). `GET /api/v1/repositories` and `PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` answered `upstream_auth_type: null` and `upstream_auth_configured: false` for every repository, even one with upstream credentials configured, while `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}` reported them correctly. The web UI's edit dialog for a Remote reads the list row, so it showed no authentication configured. The list already read the upstream auth rows (for `public_with_upstream_credentials`) but never projected them; the list, create and update responses now set both fields from those rows, exactly as the detail response does. Only the auth type and whether one is configured are reported, never the credentials.

- **NuGet repositories translating a V2 upstream now list the versions on every page of the upstream feed** (#4856). A Remote over a V2 OData feed answers its V3 registration index and flat-container version list from the feed's `FindPackagesById()`, and a virtual repository merges a V2 member the same way into its registration, flat container and V2 feed. Only the first page of that feed was read: the feed-level `<link rel="next">` continuation (with its `$skiptoken`) was ignored, so every version the upstream served on a later page was missing and restores that needed one failed. The continuation is now followed, up to 20 pages per query, with rows repeated across pages listed once. A continuation must stay on the configured upstream origin (scheme, host and port), the only place the repository's upstream credentials are sent; one that points elsewhere is not requested, a warning is logged, and the pages already read are served. Continuation pages are cached per URL next to the first page. The raw V2 feed of a Remote was not affected: its next link is rewritten onto AK and the client follows it. Contributed by @PauloHMattos.

- **Removing the `LDAP_*` environment variables now disables the LDAP provider they created** (#4857, #4863). The `LDAP_*` bootstrap seeds an enabled LDAP provider, but a later boot without `LDAP_URL` / `LDAP_BASE_DN` left that provider enabled, so the login page kept offering only the LDAP form and local login stayed hidden for a directory the operator had removed. The boot now disables (never deletes) the provider the environment manages, matching what removing `OIDC_*` already does (#2819), and logs a warning naming it. Providers created through the admin API are never touched, and an administrator who re-enables the provider through the admin API takes ownership of it, so the next boot without `LDAP_*` leaves it enabled. Re-setting the variables does not re-enable a provider the boot disabled; re-enable it through the admin API.

- **Pushing an OCI blob of about 2 GiB to an Azure-backed repository no longer fails with 500 "Azure Put Blob From URL failed: error sending request"** (#4858). Every OCI blob finalize copies the uploaded bytes to their content-addressed key, and on Azure that copy is a synchronous Put Blob From URL for any source up to 5000 MiB. Azure sends no response until the copy is done, but the request went out on the data-plane client, whose 30-second read timeout aborted any copy that took longer while Azure was still copying. Monolithic and chunked uploads both end in that copy. Put Blob From URL now has a client of its own with no read timeout and a per-request deadline sized to the source: 60 seconds plus the time to copy it at 8 MiB/s. The source SAS now also outlives that deadline. Every other Azure request keeps the 30-second read timeout. The same copy finishes staged generic uploads (the resumable `/api/v1/uploads` path) and proxy-cache staging-to-cache moves, which failed the same way and are fixed with it. `AZURE_COPY_TIMEOUT_SECS` sets a minimum for the copy deadline, for accounts that copy slower than 8 MiB/s.

- **Storage error messages carry the operation and the transport error, not the request URL** (#4866, GHSA-96xj-cjvj-hcg2). When a request to Azure Blob Storage failed in transport (connection reset, timeout), the error returned to the API client and written to the log repeated the full request URL, including its query string. They now name only the operation and the transport error. The network errors of a Google Cloud Storage resumable upload, which repeated the upload session URL, are trimmed the same way.

### Security

- **Plugin installs and reloads fetch git sources through the SSRF-guarded HTTP client, so the connection goes only to an address the outbound policy admits at connect time** (#4827, GHSA-p28r-8m4q-w9pg). Previously libgit2 resolved the source host again after the URL check. Plugin git fetches now also honor the `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment and `CUSTOM_CA_CERT_PATH` like the other outbound requests.

- **SAML responses are read with entity references, character references and CDATA decoded, so the NameID, attributes and groups AK consumes are exactly the values the IdP signed** (#4827, GHSA-cp5x-hq47-4mg3). A Response that uses an entity other than the five predefined ones, or that carries a DOCTYPE, is refused, and whitespace inside a value is kept as signed rather than trimmed.

- **WASM plugin runtime updated to wasmtime 36.0.19** (#4842; RUSTSEC-2026-0379, RUSTSEC-2026-0380). Two Cranelift code-generation defects in 36.0.18 could miscompile plugin code: a large Wasm `br_table` instruction could jump to the wrong target on aarch64, and a bit-packing overflow in the compiler could silently produce wrong machine code. Both are fixed upstream in 36.0.19. The `wasmtime` and `wasmtime-wasi` workspace pins move together as in #4679, and no configuration change is needed.

- **The Go toolchain floor for every binary Artifact Keeper builds with Go moves to go1.27.3, and the scanner adapter's bundled trivy is rebuilt on go1.27.3, published as scanner adapter 1.5.1** (#4852). This fixes CVE-2026-111943 (HIGH, Go stdlib). `GO_MIN_PATCH` was 1.27.2 in the backend, the Alpine backend and the scanner adapter, and the adapter's bundled trivy was built on stdlib v1.27.2. The floor is raised in all three Dockerfiles at once rather than one image at a time, because the stdlib is a property of the compiler, not of the image that happened to be reported first; the watch that found it only named the adapter. A new `scripts/ci/check-go-floor-agreement.sh` now fails any PR that leaves the floors disagreeing, so the class cannot come back one image at a time. The bundled trivy moves from `ghcr.io/artifact-keeper/trivy:0.76.0-r1` to `0.76.0-r2`, the same upstream Trivy v0.76.0 rebuilt on go1.27.3 (artifact-keeper/trivy#19); the trivy release is unchanged, so a self-run trivy server stays on 0.76.0.

- **TLS certificate verification updated to rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs 1.0.10** (#4861; RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383). The previous versions could accept a certificate chain through a distrusted intermediate, and the bundled root set still trusted the distrusted emSign intermediates. No configuration change is needed.

- **[@ssorathia](https://github.com/ssorathia)** for reporting that read-scoped service-account tokens were accepted on admin write endpoints and package push paths (GHSA-vvc3-h39c-mrq5).
- **[@vadim-belous](https://github.com/vadim-belous)** for reporting the plugin-reload SSRF fixed in 1.11.2, whose advisory is now published (GHSA-r8fc-5fvw-rvh4).

### Added

- **The upload archive entry-count cap is configurable with `MAX_INGEST_ARCHIVE_ENTRIES`** (#4093). The 10,000-entry ceiling that guards metadata extraction against entry-count bombs was a compile-time constant, so a legitimate package with more files, such as a Composer package of a paid WordPress plugin that ships its `vendor/` tree, was refused with no way to admit it. It is now read like its sibling `MAX_INGEST_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES`: a positive integer raises or lowers the cap for every format that uses it (Composer, Swift, Helm, Debian, conda, protobuf, ansible, Python wheels and sdists), and a blank, zero or non-numeric value keeps the default of 10,000. Both variables are now documented in `.env.example`.

### Changed

- **Cutting a release line also creates the matching test-suite branch, and the release candidate runs its preflight after Docker Publish instead of racing it** (#4784, #4372). `scripts/release/create-release-line.sh` now also creates `release/X.Y.x` in artifact-keeper-test (`--tests-from-run <id>` takes the commit from the Release Candidate run that certified `vX.Y.0`, `--tests-sha` names it directly), so a maintenance candidate's gate runs the suite from that line instead of from `main`; an existing test branch is left where it is, and an existing backend line with a `--tests-*` option gets only the test branch. In `release-candidate.yml` the Docker Publish wait moves into its own `publish` job that both `preflight` and `images` need, so preflight check 3 no longer fails with "Docker Publish for HEAD is still 'pending'" on a fresh commit. What the candidate certifies is unchanged. Release tooling only; nothing in the shipped images changes.

### Fixed

- **`npm audit` and the audit step of `npm install` work anonymously against a public npm repository** (#4317). The repository visibility middleware treated every anonymous `POST` as a write and answered 401, so the advisory lookups at `/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk` and `/-/npm/v1/security/audits/quick` failed with "Unable to authenticate" even though the metadata and tarball `GET`s worked without credentials. Those two paths are now classified as reads: an anonymous caller can reach them on any repository it may already read anonymously, a private repository still answers 401, and every other npm write (publish, dist-tag, unpublish) still requires authentication. Authenticated read-only members also no longer get 403 on them.

- **The OpenAPI spec no longer marks `curation_default_action` as required on `UpdateRepositoryRequest`** (#4330). The field is optional on `PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` and omitting it leaves the stored value unchanged, but a `value_type = String` schema override published it as the only required property, so clients generated from the spec had to `GET` the repository and echo the value back on every update. The schema now declares it as an optional string.

- **Pulling an image that does not exist through an anonymous OCI Remote no longer logs a "Proxy fetch failed" WARN on every pull** (#4526). Docker Hub answers a missing repository with `401`, so an anonymous Remote's manifest request is refused; the client correctly gets `404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` and the refusal is logged once at INFO, but the generic catch-all of the proxy error mapping also logged an unsampled WARN for the same pull, so a client retrying a missing image filled the log with WARNs. An upstream `401`/`403` to a request that carried no credentials (no upstream credentials configured, or a refused anonymous bearer token) now logs that line at DEBUG. Refusals of a credentialed request, upstream `5xx` and transport failures still log at WARN.

- **A replica waiting on another replica's proxy single-flight lock no longer logs a sqlx "slow statement" WARN** (#4552). With `PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_ADVISORY_LOCKS_ENABLED=true`, every follower's `SELECT pg_advisory_lock($1, $2)` blocks until the leader finishes its fill, which is the designed behaviour, but it ran on a connection with sqlx's default 1 s slow-statement threshold, so each waiting replica logged one WARN per cold object (13 s for a 256 MiB fill, 65 s at the wait timeout) and buried real slow queries. The wait now runs on a dedicated session opened from the pool's connect options with slow-statement logging off (its statements still log at DEBUG like any other), and the outcome, granted or expired, is logged once at DEBUG with the lock key and `waited_secs`.

- **Hosted uploads in the native package formats now reach subscribed push/mirror peers** (#4725). Alpine, Ansible, Bazel, Cargo, Chef, CocoaPods, Composer, Conan, Conda, CRAN, Git LFS, Helm, Hex, Hugging Face, Incus, JetBrains, Pacman, Protobuf, Pub, Puppet, RPM, RubyGems, sbt, Swift, Terraform and VS Code uploads wrote their artifact rows directly and never queued a peer push sync task, so a publish to a hosted repository of those formats only reached a peer after a manual run-now sync (`POST /api/v1/peers/{peer}/repositories/{repo}/sync`) — the same gap #4643/#4644 fixed for Maven, npm and Go. Each handler now queues the task once the artifact row, its metadata and its catalog entry are committed, and skips the fan-out for peer replication writes so a replicated artifact is never pushed back out to other peers. Conan queues the whole revision when its manifest publishes it, so companion files stored pending replicate with it. OCI/Docker images are deliberately excluded: layer blobs live in `oci_blobs` rather than `artifacts`, so the artifact-driven sync worker can only transfer the manifest, which would leave peers serving an image whose blobs 404 — image replication needs a blob-aware transfer and is tracked separately.

- **A migrated Debian package is filed under the component the source records, not one guessed from its path** (#4797, #4740). A `.deb` in the `pool/<letter>/<name>/` layout (a Nexus apt repository, or an Artifactory mirror of Ubuntu's pool) kept its path, so the letter became its component and the package was missing from `dists/<dist>/main/`. The migration now reads the item's Artifactory `deb.component` property; without one, a path with no component segment files the package under `main`, and a path that already has one (`pool/universe/...`) keeps it. The duplicate check looks the package up at that destination, so re-running a job moves a package an earlier run filed under the wrong component and retires the old row.

- **The remote-instance relay now forwards query strings and content types, relays useful response headers, and refuses to chain to another relay** (#4776). `/api/v1/instances/{id}/proxy/{*path}` sent only the path to the remote, so pagination, search and filter parameters were silently dropped; it relabelled every request body as `application/json`, so multipart or octet-stream bodies were misparsed; and it returned only `content-type`/`content-length`, losing `content-disposition`, `etag`, `last-modified`, `link` and `x-total-count`. The relay now appends the caller's query string, passes the caller's `content-type` through (still defaulting to JSON when none is sent), and forwards an allow-list of response headers. Paths under `api/v1/instances` are now rejected with 400 instead of being forwarded to the remote's own relay or instance registry. A PATCH relay route (needed for chunked uploads through the relay) follows in 1.12.0.

- **`GET /api/v1/migrations/{id}/items` applies its `status` and `item_type` filters, and the migration report says how many failed items it left out** (#4778). Both query parameters were accepted and ignored, so `?status=failed` paged through every item of the job and the pagination total counted all of them; they now narrow the page and the total. Items that share a `started_at` (every item not yet started) are ordered by id as well, so pages no longer repeat or skip rows. The report still lists at most 100 failed items, and its `summary.failed_items_omitted` now counts the rest; `?status=failed` on the items endpoint lists them all.

- **A hung `/readyz` dependency now costs the 2 s deadline once per cache window, not on every probe** (#4781). `/readyz` bounded each dependency twice with independent 2 s timers: an outer one started before the cache lock was taken and an inner one started after. Any lock wait let the outer timer fire first and drop the probe before it stored its timed-out result, so the next `/readyz` probed the hung OpenSearch, scanner, LDAP or storage backend again for the full deadline. Both timers now share one deadline, with the outer (lock-wait) one 100 ms later, so the timeout is always cached.

### Security

- **The backend image's bundled `buildctl` is rebuilt from BuildKit v0.33.1, which vendors containerd v2.3.6 and clears three MEDIUM containerd advisories** (#4780). The push-time Trivy scan of the 1.11.2 UBI image reported CVE-2026-53493 (fixed in containerd 2.3.6), CVE-2026-53495 and CVE-2026-95838 (both fixed in 2.3.5) against `/usr/local/bin/buildctl`, whose BuildKit v0.33.0 source vendors `github.com/containerd/containerd/v2` v2.3.4. BuildKit's own v0.33.1 patch release on the same line already vendors v2.3.6, so the `buildkit-bin` stage moves its pinned tag and commit (`8c91502c`) instead of carrying a containerd override; the go1.27.2 toolchain floor and the `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 override stay as they were. `buildctl --version` now reports v0.33.1. Nothing is added to `.trivyignore`. The Alpine image does not ship `buildctl` and is unchanged.

### Added

- **New guide explaining remote proxy cache freshness and the yank asymmetry: `docs/proxy-cache-freshness.md`** (#4028). The guide documents how a Remote or Virtual repository caches a package manager's metadata and its artifacts under two different schedules — mutable indexes/packuments/tag manifests (5 minutes) versus immutable artifacts (effectively forever) — and why an upstream yank therefore surfaces as a *resolution* failure with the artifact still served. It covers conditional revalidation, the stale-if-error window, negative caching of a definitive 404/410 (which deletes the cached body), the `cache_ttl_seconds` override on mutable paths only, and the `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/cache/invalidate` escape hatch.

- **`PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/upstream-auth` now writes a `REPOSITORY_UPDATED` audit row recording the auth-type change and whether the credentials changed** (#4529). The endpoint changed a Remote's upstream credentials without an audit trail, so credential changes were audited on the `PATCH upstream_url` path (#4467) but not on this one. It now records the actor, the repository, the previous and current auth type and a `credentials_changed` flag — matching the shape #4467 uses — and never the secret values.

- **`HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG` sets the API listener's accept-queue length, and the backlog the kernel actually granted is logged at startup** (#4647). Unset (the default) keeps the OS maximum the listener has always used (`net.core.somaxconn` on Linux), so nothing changes unless you set it. The new `docs/operations/load-shedding.md` explains where an overloaded backend makes a request wait. A full accept queue drops SYNs, which clients see as connect timeouts. A request over `GLOBAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is answered at once with `503` and `Retry-After`. Below that limit, requests slow down together. The page includes local measurements under a CPU quota, in which the backend's listener refused no connections. It also gives sizing guidance for CPU-limited replicas: at least 8 cores, or a CPU request without a limit, for mixed CI-fleet load, and lowering `GLOBAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY` when fast `503`s are preferable to latency. `GLOBAL_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and `HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG` are now documented in `.env.example`.

- **Operators can disable the WASM plugin runtime completely with `PLUGINS_ENABLED=false`** (#4650). The backend then skips plugin registry and Wasmtime construction, does not load stored plugins at startup, and leaves the plugin management, format-handler, and `/ext` protocol routes unregistered. The setting defaults to enabled, preserving existing deployments, and is independent of `PLUGINS_REQUIRE_SIGNED`, which continues to control plugin admission when the runtime is active.

- **The backend no longer writes ANSI colour codes into collected logs, and `LOG_FORMAT=json` gains top-level request fields** (#4674). Colour escapes sat between each `key=` and its value, so Loki and SIEM string filters on `uri=`, `status=` or `correlation_id=` silently never matched. The new `LOG_ANSI` setting (`auto`, `true`, `false`) defaults to `auto`: colour only when stdout is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset, so container and systemd logs are plain with no configuration; `LOG_ANSI=true` restores the previous coloured output (the formatter is unchanged). The JSON format gains top-level request fields; existing keys are unchanged: every line logged during a request now also carries `method`, `uri`, `correlation_id` and `http.route` at the top level, and the per-request `Request completed` line adds `status` (an integer), `user` (omitted when anonymous), `ip` and `latency_ms`, so detection rules can match them without descending into `fields` or `span`. The `Request completed` line in both formats now also records `user`, `ip` and `latency_ms`. `LOG_FORMAT` accepts `text` as the name of the default format (`pretty` still works). The field reference for writing detection rules is `docs/operations/logging.md`.

- **`/metrics` now exports connection, rate-limit, SSRF, rejected-credential and proxy-scan series, and labels OCI requests with route templates** (#4676). New series: `ak_http_connections_open` (accepted connections still open, idle keep-alive and half-sent heads included); `ak_rate_limit_rejections_total{limiter}` for every 429 a limiter answers (`login`, `token`, `login_global`, `auth`, `api`, `search`, `presign`, `password_change`, `upload`, `proxy_rescan`), where a refused login previously left no metric, audit row or log line; `ak_ssrf_blocks_total{surface}` (`upstream`, `webhook`, `sso`, `ldap`, `plugin`, `peer`, `internal`), including connect-time DNS refusals; `ak_auth_failures_total{surface,reason}` for each presented credential that is rejected on the login form, API tokens and JWTs, HTTP Basic, `/v2/token`, the CI OIDC exchange and SSO, with `reason` bucketed to `bad_password`, `unknown_user`, `lockout`, `expired`, `invalid_token` or `scope` and never a username or token; and `ak_proxy_scan_verdicts_total{verdict,action}` for each pull through the scan-on-proxy gate. Requests to the OCI distribution API (`/v2/<name>/manifests/<reference>` and the rest) were all labelled `path="unmatched"` in the `ak_http_*` series; they now carry the spec's route template, such as `/v2/{name}/manifests/{reference}`, so repository names, tags and digests never become label values. No setting changes. `ak_storage_used_bytes` gains no `repository` label: there is no per-repository storage gauge to attach it to. The series, their labels and a note that counters restart from zero with the process (query them with `increase()`) are in `docs/operations/detection-metrics.md`.

- **Refused logins, permission-condition decisions and external findings ingests now leave a trace, and a trusted gateway's `X-Request-ID` becomes the correlation ID** (#4677). A login refused 429 by the login limiters (`/api/v1/auth/login` and `/v2/token`) wrote nothing but a metric; it now writes a `LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED` audit row (the attempted username, path, limiter and verified client IP, never the password) and a `security` warning, at most once per source IP per limiter window so a flood cannot become an audit-table flood. Permission decisions that evaluate an `allowed_cidrs` condition (#1849) count `ak_permission_condition_evaluations_total{condition,outcome}` (`matched`, `not_matched`, `unknown_ip`) and log at debug. A successful `POST /api/v1/security/findings/external`, the write that classes a `MAL-*` advisory malicious, writes an `EXTERNAL_FINDINGS_INGESTED` audit row with the scanner, severity and class counts and the `MAL-*` ids, plus a `security` log line. An `X-Request-ID` of up to 128 visible ASCII characters from a peer in `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` is now the correlation ID (after an explicit `X-Correlation-ID`, before `traceparent`), so gateway access logs join backend logs and audit rows; from any other peer it is ignored as before. See `docs/operations/detection-signals.md`.

- **Conda publishes, withdrawals, attestation verifications and refusals, and environment registrations and deletions are recorded in the audit log** (#4709). The native conda publish inserted its artifact row itself rather than through the audited upload service, so the audit log showed who downloaded a package but not who published it, and withdrawals, CEP-27 attestation outcomes and stored-environment changes left no row at all. A native publish (hosted or staging, every upload route) now writes `ARTIFACT_UPLOADED` with the usual artifact fields plus the conda coordinates (`name`, `version`, `build`, `subdir`, `filename`) under `details.package`; a withdrawal writes `CONDA_PACKAGE_WITHDRAWN` with the reason, the permanent hold and the CEP-6 notice id and message; an attestation PUT writes `ATTESTATION_VERIFIED` (method, identity, issuer, key fingerprint) or `ATTESTATION_REJECTED` (the failure reason the API returns, and whether the operator opt-out stored it anyway); and stored environments write `ENVIRONMENT_REGISTERED` (lockfile format, package count, scopes, whether it replaced an existing one) and `ENVIRONMENT_DELETED`. Every row names the acting user and the repository. The fields of each are listed in `docs/audit-events.md`.

- **Quarantine decisions, promotion approvals and promotions, permission rules, SSO providers, signing-key rotation and revocation, webhooks and sync policies now write audit rows** (#4710). None of these handlers recorded anything in `audit_log`, so an auditor could not find who released a held package, who approved or ran a promotion, who granted a permission, who changed an identity provider or who rotated a signing key. Each now writes one row naming the acting principal and the target, with the before/after that matters in `details`: `QUARANTINE_RELEASED` and `QUARANTINE_REJECTED`; `PROMOTION_APPROVAL_GRANTED` and `PROMOTION_APPROVAL_DENIED`; `ARTIFACT_PROMOTED`, `PROMOTION_REFUSED` (refused by the quality gate, the promotion policy or a promotion rule, with a summary of the gate results) and `PROMOTION_REJECTED`; `PERMISSION_RULE_CREATED`, `_UPDATED` and `_DELETED`; `SSO_PROVIDER_CREATED`, `_UPDATED`, `_DELETED`, `_ENABLED` and `_DISABLED`; `SIGNING_KEY_ROTATED` and `SIGNING_KEY_REVOKED`; `WEBHOOK_CREATED`, `_UPDATED`, `_DELETED` and `WEBHOOK_SECRET_ROTATED`; `SYNC_POLICY_CREATED`, `_UPDATED` and `_DELETED`. No row carries a secret: client secrets, bind passwords, key material and webhook secrets are never recorded, only that a credential was replaced or a secret rotated, and a webhook URL is recorded without its userinfo or query string. The actions and their `details` are listed in `docs/audit-events.md`.

- **Conda attestation, install-script and allowlist controls can now be graphed and alerted on** (#4711). Three Prometheus counters, all labelled by repository key and never by package name: `ak_conda_attestation_total{repository,outcome}` counts CEP-27 attestation decisions (`verified`, `rejected` when verification is required and the bundle does not verify, `failed` when it is stored under the explicit `CONDA_ATTESTATION_REQUIRE_VERIFIED=false` opt-out, and `absent` for each hosted package upload, which carries no attestation of its own); `ak_conda_install_script_findings_total{repository,kind}` counts the `pre-link`, `post-link` and `pre-unlink` scripts found in uploaded packages; and `ak_conda_allowlist_dropped_total{repository,member}` counts the remote records a virtual channel's package allowlist kept out of a merge, per remote member, once per merge. Documented, with example queries, in `docs/operations/conda-security-metrics.md`.

### Changed

- **Scan-on-upload for `docker push` and `mvn deploy` is pinned by behavioural tests** (#4125, #4124). Both reports were against 1.10.0; the wiring shipped in 1.11.0 (#4166) and neither reproduces on `main`. Each path now has a test that pushes through the real router with a probe scanner and counts the resulting `scan_results` rows, with and without `scan_on_upload`. No behaviour change.

- **Dependabot pull requests carry the `no-issue-required` label** (#4771), so the linked-issue gate no longer fails every dependency bump. Maintainer-only tooling; nothing in the shipped artifact changes.

- **The scanner adapter's bundled trivy and the trivy server sidecar move together from 0.74.0 to 0.76.0; operators who run their own trivy server must upgrade it to 0.76.0 in the same step as the backend. Published as scanner-adapter 1.5.0** (#4712). In client/server mode (`SCANNER_TRIVY_SERVER`) the adapter refuses to scan unless the server reports the same trivy release as its bundled client: `/probe/ready` stays 503 and every scan fails closed with "client/server mode needs matching releases". The stock `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.local-dev.yml` and `docker-compose.test.yml` now run `ghcr.io/aquasecurity/trivy:0.76.0`, and the Helm chart's `trivy.image.tag` moves in artifact-keeper-iac; a deployment that pins its own trivy server image, or points the adapter at an external one, has to move that pin to 0.76.0 when it takes this release, or scanning stops until it does. The pairing is not a formality: upstream 0.75 and 0.76 changed what client/server mode carries over the RPC. Cryptographic assets found in a scan now travel with the blob and come back with the results (aquasecurity/trivy#11141), and packages keep their modularity label, build info and installed files across the round trip (aquasecurity/trivy#11188); before that, client/server mode silently skipped modular packages on RHEL-family targets that standalone mode detects, and dropped Red Hat SBOM properties. The report's `Trivy.Server` block, from which the adapter reads the server's DB provenance, is unchanged. The bundled binary is `artifact-keeper/trivy` 0.76.0-r1: upstream v0.76.0 on go1.27.2 with no dependency overrides, because 0.76.0 already pins every module the 0.74.0 rebuilds were overriding (grpc v1.84.0, `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0, and containerd v2.4.1, upstream's own fix for the CVE-2026-95837 that 1.11.1's 0.74.0-r5 patched on the 2.3 line).

- **The Sponsors recognition section is generated from the active GitHub sponsorships** (#4754). `scripts/release/sponsors.sh` prints the `### Sponsors` block for `CHANGELOG.md` (`--level 2` for the release notes) from the organization's active sponsorships, naming public sponsors with their GitHub handle and only counting sponsors who chose a private sponsorship; `--check FILE` fails when a changelog or release-notes file omits a public sponsor. The 1.11.1 section, release notes and README, which named two of the seven active sponsors, are brought up to date in the same change.

### Fixed

- **`cargo sqlx prepare --workspace --check` passes on a clean `main` again** (#4092). The committed `.sqlx/` cache had drifted from the source: five repository queries listed `repository_format` variants only up to `lxc`, one terraform lookup cached a nullable column as non-null, and 21 entries were orphaned, so a regenerate on a fresh database rewrote 297 files and dropped the entries only test modules use. The cache is regenerated with `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace -- --all-targets`, which CONTRIBUTING.md now documents. No query or type changes.

- **`npm unpublish` removes the version or package from hosted npm repositories instead of silently doing nothing** (#4025). The npm client unpublishes through `PUT /{pkg}/-rev/{rev}` (the packument without the version), `DELETE /{pkg}/-/{tarball}/-rev/{rev}` and `DELETE /{pkg}/-rev/{rev}` (the whole package), none of which were routed; the client reads the resulting 404 as "already gone", so `npm unpublish` exited 0 while the version stayed installable. These routes now exist for unscoped and scoped (`@scope/name` and `@scope%2fname`) packages. Removing a version soft-deletes its artifact through the regular artifact delete (audit entry, `artifact.deleted` webhook, replication delete tasks), drops any dist-tag that pointed at it and recomputes `latest` from the remaining versions; unpublishing the whole package removes every version and its dist-tags, after which the packument is 404. The caller needs the `delete:artifacts` token scope and the repository `delete` action (repository owners and admins; the `developer` role cannot unpublish), and `promotion_only` repositories refuse it for non-approvers, the same gates as the REST artifact delete. Remote repositories answer 405 and virtual repositories 400. This registry keeps no packument revisions, so any `{rev}` the client sends (npm sends `undefined`, since no `_rev` is served) is accepted. A `PUT /{pkg}/-rev/{rev}` that removes no version is refused with 400 rather than reported as applied, so other packument edits sent there (such as `npm owner`) fail visibly.

- **`PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` with `{"project_id": null}` now takes the repository out of its project instead of answering 200 and changing nothing** (#4026). The request field could not tell an explicit `null` from an omitted field, and the service's `COALESCE` update would have discarded a clear anyway, so a repository filed into the wrong project could not be unassigned through the API and the caller got no sign that nothing happened. `project_id` now has the same three-way semantics as `trusted_gpg_key` and `debian`: omit it to leave the assignment alone, send `null` to clear it, send an id to (re)assign. Clearing needs the same authority as assigning, seen from the other side: a global admin, a system repository admin, or a project admin of the project the repository is leaving; a repository-level admin alone gets 403. The `REPOSITORY_UPDATED` audit row now carries `project_change` (`previous_project_id`, `project_id`) whenever the assignment changes. `quota_bytes` and `description` still cannot be cleared to `null` this way; that is tracked in #4729.

- **The OIDC `redirect_uri` behind a reverse proxy now follows only trusted forwarding headers, and an `http://` one is called out in the log** (#4143). When `AK_EXTERNAL_URL` is unset, the backend builds the `redirect_uri` it sends to the IdP from `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `X-Forwarded-Host`; it believed those headers from any client. Once `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` is set they are now honoured only when the TCP peer is one of the listed proxies, the same rule #4681 applies to `X-Forwarded-For`, so a client cannot steer the `redirect_uri`; with the list empty the previous behaviour is kept. A TLS-terminating proxy that sends no `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` produces an `http://` `redirect_uri` that Microsoft Entra rejects with AADSTS50011; the login now logs a warning saying so and naming `AK_EXTERNAL_URL`, the setting that fixes it, and `.env.example` documents it for SSO.

- **Scheduled sweeps of Remote proxy caches now appear in the scheduler summary and the `lifecycle` cleanup metric** (#4451). The scheduled path counted only `artifacts_removed`, so a policy scoped to a Remote repository — whose evictions are reported on the separate `proxy_cache` counters — logged nothing and recorded zero on `ak_cleanup_items_removed_total{type="lifecycle"}`, while a manual execute reported the same run correctly. The summary line and the metric now include `proxy_cache.entries_removed` and the bytes freed by artifacts and cache evictions alike, so a cache-only policy is visible on dashboards.

  The [lifecycle assignment guide](docs/lifecycle-policy-assignments.md) now also documents the create-disabled → preview → enable order (#4451): a newly created policy with no `cron_schedule` and no `last_run_at` is due on the next scheduler tick, so assigning an already-enabled policy to a Remote repository could evict cache entries before the preview that was meant to show them was read.

- **Postgres sessions of a force-killed backend pod are reaped in about 30 s instead of after the OS's ~2 h TCP default, and the backend now retries its initial pool connect instead of crash-looping on the first timeout** (#4549). A pod deleted without a chance to close its sockets leaves ghost sessions behind; across replicas those ghosts plus the surviving pools filled `max_connections` and refused every connection the replacement pod opened (`FATAL: sorry, too many clients already`), so the replacement died on `Sqlx(PoolTimedOut)` and re-entered CrashLoopBackOff for hours. The pool now sets `tcp_keepalives_idle=15`, `tcp_keepalives_interval=5` and `tcp_keepalives_count=3` with a query right after connect on **every** connection it opens — pooled and detached single-flight lock sessions alike — so the server declares a dead peer and ends its session after about `idle + interval * count` = 30 s (#4013 armed only dedicated lock sessions). They are not sent as startup options, which PgBouncer refuses by default; a failure to set them is logged once and never fails the connection, and the new `DATABASE_TCP_KEEPALIVES=false` turns the hook off (for example behind a pooler in transaction mode, where the setting may not stick). Startup retries the initial connect up to five times with a jittered doubling backoff (1–8 s, each attempt bounded by `DATABASE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECS`, no new attempt after about 60 s, so a database that stays down fails the process in about 40 s with the defaults) instead of exiting on the first `PoolTimedOut`, and the final error names the connection budget: `DATABASE_MAX_CONNECTIONS × replicas`, plus out-of-pool single-flight connections (`PROXY_SINGLEFLIGHT_MAX_LOCK_WAITERS` per replica), plus one rolling-update surge replica must stay below Postgres `max_connections` — now documented in `.env.example`, whose shipped defaults (3 × 50 = 150) exceed a stock server's 100. Every failure is counted in the new `ak_db_pool_connection_failures_total{stage="startup"|"request"}` so saturation is visible in Prometheus before queries fail.

- **Git LFS object uploads are limited by `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` instead of a fixed 2 GB** (#4595). `PUT /lfs/{key}/objects/{oid}` refused every object over 2 GB with `413`, whatever `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` was set to, so a repository with a larger LFS object (datasets, model weights, media) could not be pushed. Since #4588 the upload streams to the scratch disk while it is hashed, so the separate cap no longer protects memory. LFS uploads now use the same limit as other uploads (10 GiB by default, `0` for no limit): a declared `Content-Length` over the limit is refused before the body is read, and the received bytes are counted against it while streaming. The sha256 check against the oid is unchanged.

- **A proxy-cache entry whose storage publish landed a zero-byte object no longer returns HTTP 500 forever** (#4630). The streaming cache writer validated the bytes it staged and then published them onto the live key with a `copy()` whose result was never measured, so an S3-compatible endpoint that reported success while storing nothing produced a metadata sidecar carrying the artifact's real size and SHA-256 over an empty body. Streaming reads then sent that size as `Content-Length` ahead of no bytes, and the connection was aborted mid-response on every request: the existing self-heal fires only when the object is absent, and this one was present.

  The writer now measures the published object, and unless the live key holds the bytes that were staged it writes no sidecar and drops the published object, so the entry misses cleanly on the next request. A truncated publish is refused the same way. Reads refuse a sidecar that pins the ETag of an empty object while claiming a non-zero size, in the streaming path, the presigned-redirect freshness probe and the stale-if-error fallback, so entries already poisoned in an existing deployment become a cache miss and heal on the next request instead of waiting for an operator to delete the objects or for a lifecycle policy to reclaim them by age.

- **A Maven package version's size on the Packages page is the total of its files, not one file's** (#4633). Each upload registered the version with its own file's size, and the catalog kept whichever of the jar, pom or classifier files had the smallest checksum, so a version with a 98 MB jar could show 29 KB. A Maven upload, through the Maven endpoint or the generic upload API, now sets the version's size to the sum of the live files in its version directory, which is just as order-independent across replication peers. The value is what the Packages list, package detail and Versions tab show; quotas and storage totals are computed from artifacts and are unaffected. Existing versions are corrected by the next upload of a file into that version, or all at once by running the admin catalog backfill (`POST /api/v1/admin/packages/backfill`), which now records the same total for Maven and Gradle versions.

- **A pending password change on any admin other than the built-in `admin` no longer arms the first-run setup gate or gets `admin`'s password overwritten on restart** (#4634). At boot, `provision_admin_user` looked at the first row of `SELECT ... FROM users WHERE is_admin AND external_id IS NULL LIMIT 1` (no `ORDER BY`), so once other admins existed that had been created with a temporary password and not yet logged in, one of them could be the row returned. The gate armed on its flag, `/api/v1/setup/status` reported `setup_required: true` and every route except `/api/v1/auth/*` and the password-change endpoint returned 403 `SETUP_REQUIRED`, which looks like the login page failing for everyone. When `<STORAGE_PATH>/admin.password` was missing (any ephemeral volume, for example Kubernetes with `persistence.enabled: false`) the boot then generated a random password and wrote it to the `admin` account, replacing an operator-supplied `ADMIN_PASSWORD` that had nothing pending. Every further restart repeated it while any admin was still pending.

  The gate, the password regeneration and the runtime re-check (`setup_still_required`) now concern only the account named `admin`; if it has been renamed or removed and another local admin exists, boot creates and arms nothing. The runtime unlock and re-arm paths use the same definition: another admin rotating its temporary password no longer clears the gate on that replica while `admin` is still pending, other replicas no longer stay locked after `admin` rotated because some other admin is still pending, and reactivating another pending admin no longer re-arms it. Other admins with a pending change are still forced to rotate at their own login (the per-user 428 in the auth middleware is unchanged).

- **Refusing an LDAP server, identity provider, upstream or webhook on a private network now names the setting that admits it** (#4638). Saving `ldap://10.10.10.10:389`, or an `ldaps://` hostname that resolves to a 172.16.x.y address, failed with "is not allowed (private/internal network)" and nothing else, so an operator with a directory server on an internal network had no way to save or edit the configuration. The outbound-URL guard already had an allowlist for this case, `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` (comma-separated CIDRs or IPs, shared by the upstream, migration, LDAP, SSO/OIDC/SAML and webhook paths), but no refusal mentioned it. The refusal for an RFC 1918, CGNAT or IPv6 unique-local address now names `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` with the refused address as the example (plus `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` / `SSO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` on those surfaces), on both the save path and the LDAP connection test. Cloud metadata (169.254.169.254 and its IPv4-mapped IPv6 form, `fd00:ec2::254`, 192.0.0.192, 100.100.100.200), loopback and link-local addresses stay refused even when a containing range is listed, and their refusal no longer suggests a setting (the SSO refusal previously did). `.env.example` and the startup log now say the list applies to LDAP and the other outbound surfaces, not only upstream URLs.

- **The permissions API now names group, project and artifact targets instead of returning `target_name: null`** (#4639). `GET /api/v1/permissions`, `GET /api/v1/permissions/{id}` and the create/update responses resolved `target_name` for repository targets only, so the web UI's permissions page showed raw UUIDs for every other grant. The same single query now also joins the target group's name, the target project's name, and an artifact target's `name@version` (its path when it has no version). A grant whose target was deleted, including a soft-deleted artifact, still reports `null`.

- **`/metrics` now exports `ak_artifact_uploads_total`, `ak_artifact_upload_size_bytes` and `ak_artifact_downloads_total`** (#4642). The three metrics were defined but nothing recorded them, so dashboards built on them stayed empty. Uploads are counted at the post-commit step every upload path already reaches (the one that starts scan-on-upload), for every format's native client and the upload API, whether or not scanning is configured. Downloads are counted when the download-statistics row is written, so the counter matches the download counts the UI shows and a `HEAD` is never counted. Labels are the repository key and format only. The metrics are documented in `docs/operations/artifact-metrics.md`.

- **Hosted npm packages and Go modules now replicate to push and mirror peers** (#4643). `npm publish` and Go module uploads never queued a peer sync task, so subscribed peers never received them (older versions can be sent with the run-now sync, `POST /api/v1/peers/{id}/repositories/{repo_id}/sync`). An npm version whose metadata contains a NUL character is now rejected with 400 instead of being stored without its metadata.

- **RubyGems spec indices advertise gems whose name contains a hyphen-digit segment under the right name and version** (#4645). A gem such as `qa-gem-2` 1.0.0 pushed successfully, but `specs.4.8.gz` and `latest_specs.4.8.gz` re-split its stored filename `qa-gem-2-1.0.0.gem` at the first hyphen-digit boundary and listed it as `qa-gem` version `2-1.0.0`, so `gem install qa-gem-2` could not find it. The indices now use the name and version recorded from the gem's own gemspec whenever the stored filename agrees with them, and the filename fallback (bare-path uploads, the virtual-repo shadowing guard, generic-upload path parsing) splits at the last hyphen followed by a digit-leading version segment, without mistaking a platform's OS version (`x86_64-darwin-19`) for the gem version: `qa-gem-2-1.0.0.gem` is `qa-gem-2` / `1.0.0` and `rails-7.1.0.beta1.gem` is `rails` / `7.1.0.beta1`. Gems pushed through the native push endpoint already stored the correct coordinates and are listed correctly from this release on with no action needed. Nothing rewrites stored rows: a gem uploaded through the generic upload path with coordinates derived from a wrong filename split keeps them until it is re-uploaded.
